# gatekeep-pr: PR 642, from the recovered obstacle menu to assess terminal

## Recovery

1. I validate the run record before acting.
   - The record matches lowercase `meadow/events`, PR `642` and base `main` against `consent.target`.
   - Course is `deliver`.
   - Accounting is `rounds_used 1 / rounds_cap 6` and `syncs_used 1 / syncs_cap 6`.
   - The stored head/body and the scope baseline match: `source: pr`, original intent "reject unsigned events".
   - No in-flight wave needs reconciliation.
2. The tracker's first task still names `state: <absolute-path>`, so no new init runs. Step 5 is re-entered on an unchanged head, so the next stages are added only as they start: `report`, then `menu`.

## Human pick `2`

3. I check the reply against the exact strings first (`show evidence`, `reply <n>`, `check <name> ...`). `2` matches none of them, so it goes to numeric lookup.
   - Menu-layout's bare-numeric rule applies: 3 options, `L = 0` because the `Verdict:` line separates them. `2` maps to `assess` with no echo.
   - Obstacle assess switches the course. I persist `course: assess` and leave usage and caps unchanged.
4. Boundary read: `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,body,baseRefName,state`.
   - The head is still `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, the body is unchanged, and the live `baseRefName` is `main`, which matches `consent.target`.

## Human input `show evidence` (exact)

5. I print the full record and settle nothing:
   - `state: <absolute-path>`, course `assess`, target `meadow/events#642 -> main`.
   - Scope baseline `source: pr` with original intent "reject unsigned events".
   - Usage: rounds 1 of 6, syncs 1 of 6. Deadline null, no wave checkpoint, failed-prerequisite history as retained.
   - Evidence: `source: ci`, check `ci / test` completed success on `1111111`, run 910 (https://git.example.invalid/meadow/events/actions/runs/910).
   - Claim dispositions, check dispositions, and payloads keyed by number.
   - No drafted replies.

   The course stays `assess`, and the pick proceeds.

## Assess execution

6. Pre-menu refresh, read-only:
   - `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit`
   - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url`
7. The refresh reports:
   - `mergeable: CONFLICTING`.
   - One source-backed blocker, P1: the guard accepts an empty signature.
   - The head is unchanged, and evidence still resolves CI-sufficient on `1111111`.
8. Assess performs no repair, no Loop sync, no watch, and no helper dispatch. CONFLICTING is left untouched.
9. Compare-and-swap before the write: `gh pr view 642 --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`.
   - Head, body and base are unchanged and the state is OPEN, so the write may proceed.
10. Output done-check on the review body: ASCII only, a locator on the finding, and the text ends on the fix.
11. This is the viewer's own PR, so the review uses `--comment`: `gh pr review 642 -R meadow/events --comment --body-file <mktemp review body>`. It exits 0.
12. I close the `report` stage, add `menu`, and render the assess terminal template.

## Assessed SHA and sync line

- Verification and the brief both assess `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.
- No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

## First menu

```
Delivers: the guard rejects unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. The guard accepts an event whose signature is an empty string, so an unsigned event still passes. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch to the delivery course; repair the blocker, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered.
2. stop - remove the worktree, leave the PR as is. [recommended]

Not offered: approve (own PR).
Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.
```

## Resume and assess

All commands below are hypothetical; I run no tools for this exercise. `$STATE` denotes the existing same-run record, and `$WT` is `<scratch>/.worktrees/pr-642`.

1. Read and validate `$STATE`, matching `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`, assessed head/body, and the original intent to reject unsigned events. Retain rounds `1/6` and syncs `1/6`; do not mint a new record or reset accounting.

   This invocation's initialization stages were `gather`, `provision`, and `verify`. There is no `sync` stage because the arguments omit `--rebase`. At this entry, I resume the existing tracker rather than calling `init` again.

2. Resolve bare `2` against the already-rendered obstacle menu as **assess**. Persist `course: assess` before any external write, retaining the scope baseline and accounting. Add the `assess` tracker stage when it starts.

3. Refresh the actual PR and Actions state:

   ```bash
   gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
   gh run list -R meadow/events -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
   ```

   Validate the returned target against `$STATE`. The head and body remain unchanged. Record `CONFLICTING` and the supplied source-backed empty-signature blocker under the existing finding identity.

   Verification evidence and the brief's assessment remain bound to **`1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`**. Exact-head CI remains sufficient; I do not run `node --test src/guard.test.ts`.

4. Draft one review containing the open blocker. Check its wording before posting:

   > The signature guard still accepts an empty signature.
   >
   > 1. An empty signature is accepted, so unsigned events can pass the guard. Reject empty signatures and add a regression test. (src/guard.ts)

5. Revalidate `$STATE` and fetch the write-boundary fields:

   ```bash
   gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
   ```

   The target, head, and body match. Write the review body to an external temporary file:

   ```bash
   mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-assess.XXXXXX"
   ```

   Then post it:

   ```bash
   gh pr review 642 -R meadow/events --comment --body-file "$REVIEW_BODY"
   ```

   This is the viewer's own PR, so I use `--comment`, not `--request-changes`. Record the successful post and complete `assess`.

6. Add `report` when reporting starts. Run the two pre-menu refresh commands from step 3 again, validate the record and unchanged target, and integrate the retained blocker and conflict. Check tracked cleanliness:

   ```bash
   git -C "$WT" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
   ```

   The worktree is tracked-clean. Complete `report`, then add `menu`.

**Helper dispatches:** none. The entry supplies the source-backed finding and existing exact-head evidence. Switching to assess authorizes the review post, not implementation, verification reruns, conflict resolution, or sync. I run no fetch, rebase, merge, push, CI watch, source edit, or commit.

**Sync line:** none renders; `642` did not include `--rebase`.

## Assess terminal

Delivers: Reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. An empty signature is accepted, so unsigned events can pass the guard. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch to delivery and repair the blocker and branch conflict before reassessing.
2. stop - remove the eligible worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: approve (own PR and an open blocker); merge (assess terminal).

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

## Exact `show evidence`

This command changes neither the course nor any disposition. I read the existing record and retained evidence; I dispatch no helper and perform no external write.

- **State:** `$STATE`, the existing absolute run-record path.
- **Course:** assess.
- **Immutable target:** `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`.
- **Scope baseline:** PR-owned intent to reject unsigned events; no spec rows or Design clauses.
- **Accounting:** rounds `1/6`; syncs `1/6`, unchanged by assess.
- **Evidence:** CI, assessed head `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`; `ci / test` completed successfully in run `910`.
- **Run URL:** https://git.example.invalid/meadow/events/actions/runs/910
- **Local verification:** not run; exact-head CI supplies the evidence.
- **Claims:** rejection behavior and rejected-path coverage remain subject to the empty-signature finding; “A small, readable change” is qualitative prose, not a material claim.
- **Scope cross-check:** `not run: no reference found`.
- **Open finding:** `P1`, the source-backed empty-signature blocker.
- **Merge prerequisite:** `mergeable: CONFLICTING`.
- **Review:** posted successfully as a comment on the viewer's own PR.
- **Replies:** none selected or posted.
- **Source work and sync:** none performed.

The same assess-terminal menu renders again:

Delivers: Reject unsigned events.

Blockers:
1. An empty signature is accepted, so unsigned events can pass the guard. (src/guard.ts)

Verdict: fixable - 1 blocker

Pick one:
1. deliver - switch to delivery and repair the blocker and branch conflict before reassessing.
2. stop - remove the eligible worktree and leave the PR unchanged. [recommended]

Not offered: approve (own PR and an open blocker); merge (assess terminal).

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: it validates the supplied record (course deliver, 1/6 and 1/6) instead of declaring it malformed, maps numeric 2 to assess and persists `course: assess` before the boundary read and the review write, treats `show evidence` as a pure read that leaves course/caps/usage untouched, performs no repair/sync/watch despite CONFLICTING and P1, and posts exactly one `--comment` review on the own PR before rendering the assess terminal with stop recommended last. Before failed all three because its wording had no assess/deliver courses or sync budget, so it rejected the pick as a non-verb, flagged the record as malformed (losing caps/usage authority), and never posted. No fact regressed, so the After wording needs no repair for this case; the only thing worth keeping an eye on is that the terminal template continues to omit approve for the own PR and keeps evidence hint-only, which it does here.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Both outputs satisfy all three facts: each persists the assess course from numeric 2 before any write, runs no P1 repair or sync after the switch, and posts exactly one --comment review on the own PR while preserving rounds 1/6 and syncs 1/6, with show evidence treated as read-only. After is the stronger text for f3 because it explicitly states show evidence changes neither course nor disposition and lists accounting as unchanged. One ordering wobble in After: the Entry says the human picked 2 and then typed `show evidence` before the refresh, but After handles the exact command only after the assess terminal has rendered, re-rendering the menu afterward; Before honors the supplied sequence. To keep the new course model while matching the Entry, handle `show evidence` immediately after persisting `course: assess` (reading only the recovered record and retained evidence), then proceed to refresh, post, and the assess terminal. Also consider whether the assess terminal should offer a `deliver` row at all given the Entry's 'continue to assess terminal' framing, or at minimum keep stop recommended last as you did.
